questions.q: What does this lesson's script have in common with Lesson 13's az CLI script, structurally?
options: The same pattern — command substitution, a for loop, and an if check — since that pattern is plain bash, not az-specific
AWS CLI doesn't support for loops, only az does
Both scripts only work inside the az CLI shell
Nothing; AWS requires a completely different bash syntax
questions.explain: The command substitution, for loop, and if/else pattern is just bash — it applies to any CLI's output, az or aws.

questions.q: Why does `Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId` need two levels of [] before reaching InstanceId?
options: Because AWS nests EC2 instance data inside "reservations," one level deeper than az's flatter resource group list
Because InstanceId is a typo and should be at the top level
Because --output text requires two levels of brackets
Because AWS CLI only returns one instance per call
questions.explain: AWS's describe-instances response groups instances under Reservations[].Instances[], so the JMESPath has to walk through both levels.

questions.q: What does `--output text` do in an aws CLI command?
options: Converts the EC2 instances into text files
Only works with describe-instances, no other aws commands
Prints plain lines of values, the AWS equivalent of az's -o tsv, suitable for a bash loop
Forces the command to run in dry-run mode
questions.explain: --output text strips JSON formatting down to plain values, the same role -o tsv plays for az CLI output.

questions.q: Why does the script check `[ "$OWNER" == "None" ]` instead of `[ -z "$OWNER" ]`?
options: Because None and empty string always mean the same thing in bash
Because AWS CLI's --output text prints the literal word "None" for a missing value, not an empty string
Because -z doesn't work with AWS CLI at all
Because OWNER is always a number, never text
questions.explain: Unlike az's -o tsv, which prints nothing for a missing value, AWS CLI text output prints the literal string None.

questions.q: What does `Tags[?Key=='Owner'].Value | [0]` do in the --query filter?
options: Is invalid JMESPath syntax and will error
Finds the tag whose Key equals "Owner" and returns its Value as the first (and only) match
Returns every tag on the instance regardless of key
Deletes the Owner tag from the instance
questions.explain: ?Key=='Owner' is a JMESPath filter expression matching the tag with that key, .Value pulls its value, and | [0] takes the first match.
